title: Beta-thalassaemia
summary: Beta-thalassaemia affects how the body makes haemoglobin. People with the more serious form make too little haemoglobin and can have anaemia that needs regular care.
inheritance_plain: It is inherited in an autosomal recessive way: a child is affected only if they get a changed copy of the gene from both parents.
carrier_meaning: A carrier (beta-thalassaemia trait or minor) has one changed copy. Carriers are healthy, though some have slightly small red blood cells or mild anaemia that does not need treatment.
disease_meaning: A person with two changed copies has beta-thalassaemia. How it affects them varies; some need regular blood transfusions and specialist care.
screening: A blood test can show whether someone is a carrier. It is part of premarital screening in the UAE.
suggested_questions: My brother has beta-thalassaemia. Could I be a carrier?
What does a test for beta-thalassaemia involve?
card_summary: Reduces the body's ability to make haemoglobin. Carriers are healthy; people with two changed copies often need lifelong care.
carrier_short: One changed copy. Healthy; sometimes mild anaemia. Can pass the copy on.
disease_short: Two changed copies. A lifelong blood condition that often needs regular care.
care: Haematology clinics, genetic counselling and family support groups.
